nodes.summary: Converse to `IsInaccessible.beth_ord`: a regular beth fixed point is inaccessible. Uncountability is derived, not assumed (`aleph0_lt_of_isRegular_beth_ord`); for `x < κ`, `2 ^ x ≤ 2 ^ ℶ_{x.ord} = ℶ_{succ x.ord} < κ`, using that `κ.ord` is a limit ordinal.
nodes.title: A regular beth fixed point is inaccessible

nodes.summary: A regular beth fixed point is uncountable: regularity gives `ℵ₀ ≤ κ`, and `κ = ℵ₀` fails the fixed-point equation since `ℶ_ω > ℶ_0 = ℵ₀`.
nodes.title: A regular beth fixed point is uncountable

nodes.summary: There are at most `κ` inaccessibles below `κ`: the set injects into `↥(Set.Iio κ.ord)`, which has size `lift κ`. The `≤` half of the counting needed for the Mahlo-implies-fixed-point benchmark item.
nodes.title: At most $\kappa$ inaccessible cardinals lie below $\kappa$

nodes.summary: The fixed-point equation forces `#(inaccessibleBelow κ) = lift κ` (`card_type`): the companion to the upper bound `mk_inaccessibleBelow_le`.
nodes.title: Exactly $\kappa$ inaccessibles lie below an inaccessible fixed point

nodes.summary: If any inaccessible exists, some inaccessible has no inaccessibles below it: minimize over the initial ordinals of inaccessible cardinals (`WellFounded.has_min`), and any member of `inaccessibleBelow` would give a smaller one.
nodes.title: Existence of an inaccessible with no inaccessibles below it

nodes.summary: `κ` is inaccessible iff it is regular and a beth fixed point (uncountability is automatic by `aleph0_lt_of_isRegular_beth_ord`): this packages `of_isRegular_beth_ord` with Mathlib's `IsInaccessible.beth_ord`.
nodes.title: Inaccessible cardinals are the regular beth fixed points

nodes.summary: A cardinal κ is an *inaccessible fixed point* if κ is inaccessible and the inaccessibles below κ have order type κ (i.e. κ is the κ-th inaccessible).
nodes.title: Inaccessible fixed point

nodes.summary: Inaccessibles below an inaccessible fixed point are unbounded: if they were bounded by `a`, the set would inject into `Iic a.val`, hence have size at most `lift (a.val + 1).card < lift κ` — contradicting `mk_inaccessibleBelow`.
nodes.title: Inaccessibles are unbounded below an inaccessible fixed point

nodes.summary: Limit cardinals are unbounded below a weakly inaccessible `κ`: the sup of the `ω`-chain `μ 0 = succ (max a ℵ₀)`, `μ (n+1) = succ (μ n)` stays below `κ` (`sum_lt_of_isRegular`), exceeds `a`, and is a limit since every `x < σ` lies below some `μ n` (`exists_lt_of_lt_ciSup`).
nodes.title: Limit cardinals are unbounded below a weakly inaccessible cardinal

nodes.summary: Regular cardinals are unbounded below an uncountable limit cardinal `κ` (in particular a weakly inaccessible one): above any `a < κ` sits `succ (max a ℵ₀)`, regular by `isRegular_succ` and below `κ` since `κ` is a limit.
nodes.title: Regular cardinals are unbounded below an uncountable limit cardinal

nodes.summary: InAccBelow κ is the set of all inaccessible cardinals below κ.
nodes.title: Set of inaccessible cardinals below a cardinal

nodes.summary: The regular cardinals below `κ`, carried as initial ordinals — parallel to `inaccessibleBelow`, and definitionally the stationary set in `IsWeaklyMahlo`. Spelled with Mathlib's `Ordinal.IsInitial`.
nodes.title: Set of regular cardinals below a cardinal

nodes.summary: A strong limit `κ` is closed under cardinal exponentiation: `x ^ y ≤ 2 ^ (x * y)` (via `cantor` and `power_mul`), and `x * y < κ` by `mul_lt_of_lt`. No infiniteness hypothesis is needed — it is automatic by `IsStrongLimit.aleph0_le`.
nodes.title: Strong limit cardinals are closed under exponentiation

nodes.summary: Strong limits are unbounded below an inaccessible `κ`: above any `a < κ` sits `ℶ_{a.ord + ω}`, a strong limit by `isStrongLimit_beth` since `a.ord + ω` is a limit ordinal (`isSuccLimit_add`), and below `κ` since `(a.ord + ω).card = a.ord.card + ℵ₀ < κ` (`add_lt_of_lt`).
nodes.title: Strong limits are unbounded below an inaccessible cardinal

nodes.summary: The sup of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial: if `σ.card.ord < σ` then some member exceeds `σ.card.ord`, trapping it strictly between itself and its own initial ordinal.
nodes.title: Supremum of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial

nodes.summary: Below an inaccessible `κ`, the aleph hierarchy stays below `κ`: same argument via `IsInaccessible.aleph_ord`.
nodes.title: The aleph hierarchy stays below an inaccessible cardinal

nodes.summary: Below an inaccessible `κ`, the beth hierarchy stays below `κ`: `κ` is a beth fixed point (`IsInaccessible.beth_ord`) and `beth` is strictly monotone.
nodes.title: The beth hierarchy stays below an inaccessible cardinal

nodes.summary: Under (local) GCH, weakly inaccessible implies strongly inaccessible: for infinite `μ < κ`, `2 ^ μ = succ μ < κ` by the limit property, and the finite case is `power_lt_aleph0`.
nodes.title: Under GCH, weakly inaccessible cardinals are inaccessible

nodes.summary: For `2 ≤ x < κ` with `κ` a strong limit, `x ^< κ = κ`: every smaller power is below `κ` (`IsStrongLimit.power_lt`), while every `y < κ` sits below `2 ^ y ≤ x ^< κ`. No infiniteness hypothesis is needed — it is automatic by `IsStrongLimit.aleph0_le`.
nodes.title: Weak power below a strong limit cardinal equals the cardinal

nodes.summary: A cardinal κ is *weakly inaccessible* if it is an uncountable, regular limit cardinal.
nodes.title: Weakly inaccessible cardinal
Set Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
